title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 2:10
body: “For it cannot, it cannot be, that a man should enjoy the benefit of grace except he watch. Seest thou not what Elias saith to his disciple?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 4:27
body: “What then is one to say? That the Saints knew not all things. And this one might learn from many instances, both of the early ones, and of those who came after them, as Elisha knew not concerning the woman (2 Kings iv.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 4:43
body: “Andrew is higher minded than Philip, yet had not he attained to everything. Yet I do not think that he spake without an object, but as having heard of the miracles of the Prophets, and how Elisha wrought a sign with the loaves ( 2 Kings iv.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 5:26
body: “Mark his energy. He suffers them not even to wait for his presence, nor to receive him first and then pass the sentence of binding: but as if on the point of expelling some contagion before that it have spread itself into the rest of the body, he hastens to restrain it.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 6:17
body: “But what means "the glory as of the Only-Begotten of the Father"? Since many of the Prophets too were glorified, as this Moses himself, Elijah, and Elisha, the one encircled by the fiery chariot ( 2 Kings vi.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 9:31
body: “Seest thou his courage? Behold also the courage of John the Baptist, which he used before Herod; when he said, "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother Philip's wife." (Mark vi.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Kings 22:8
body: “Where are these words written? Why, it is said to have been "written," then also, when it is set down, not in words, but in actual events, as in the historical books ; or when the same meaning is expressed, but not in the very same words, as in this place: for the words, "They to whom it was not told about Him shall see, and they who have not heard shall understand," (Is.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
